solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Winter event in sierra — promptly take a tumble

parts.note: Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet
promptly means at once, right this moment
to take a tumble is to fall over

explanation.surface: A skier in the mountains loses their footing at once and goes sprawling in the snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow coming down is a typical seasonal weather occurrence of the coldest months.

clue.text: London area vehicle's piercing alarm

indicators.note: something piercing goes right into another thing, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: SE is south-east London, as in its postcode area
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car alarm shrieks across a London district.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a fright or sudden fear is the same feeling as being given a start by danger.

clue.text: Slogan about husband and wife drawn in toward breaking up

indicators.note: items drawn in are pulled inside something else, so they go into the middle of the jumbled word
something breaking up falls apart, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
C is short for circa, Latin for about
H is the standard abbreviation for husband
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A couple's motto about drawing closer together seems to be falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto or rallying cry adopted by a group serves exactly as a catchphrase or slogan.

clue.text: Bleak before following street paved with gold

indicators.note: in a down clue a surface paving the road lies on top of it, so this piece is placed above the next
following means coming after, so this piece is placed after the others

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
St is the abbreviation for street
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A dismal outlook comes before walking down a street whose pavement is made of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, gold paving the street sits on top of it, so the gold comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something stark, plain and severe, without comfort or ornament.

clue.text: Old Scottish character with a lot of neck, unreliably sighted

definitions.text: Old Scottish character with a lot of neck, unreliably sighted

parts.words: Old Scottish character with a lot of neck
parts.note: surface reading: a cheeky elderly Scot with plenty of nerve
setter's reading: a long-necked creature of Highland legend whose reported sightings nobody can trust

explanation.surface: A brazen old Scotsman is glimpsed here and there, though witnesses can't be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: Having a lot of neck is British slang for being cheeky; here the neck is literal, a long one rising from the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary creature of a Highland loch is pictured with a long neck, and its supposed sightings are notoriously dubious.

clue.text: Writer needs line after US VP cut one

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the surname loses its final letter
after means placed later, so the line goes at the end

parts.note: Mike Pence was US Vice-President from 2017 to 2021
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A speechwriter wants a line to follow a trimmed passage about the American vice-president.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer here is a writing implement, and this graphite stick is one such tool.

clue.text: 'Hop it,' I fulminated, putting in 'sorry!'

indicators.note: the words put in the run of text hold the letters inside them, waiting to be found

parts.note: the letters run across the end of hop, then it, I, and the start of fulminated

explanation.surface: Someone angrily shouts at another to clear off, then adds an apology.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorry can mean wretched or pathetic, as in a sorry state, which is the adjective's sense here.

clue.text: Do some decorating work — note time to go and time to stay

indicators.note: a thing that has to go is removed, so one letter is taken out

parts.note: a crotchet is a musical note, a quarter note
T is the abbreviation for time; this one leaves
padding that tells us the other time abbreviation in the note remains in place

explanation.surface: An instruction for redecorating a room: one session is off, another remains.
explanation.walkthrough: The note contains two Ts; the first goes and the second stays.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooking yarn into lace or patterned trim is needlework done to ornament fabric, so it is decorative work.

clue.text: Warren seen in bar, thinly disguised

indicators.note: a disguised thing has its appearance altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Warren is spotted in a pub wearing a flimsy disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: Warren looks like a man's name, but it is a maze of passages, like a rabbit warren.
explanation.definitionFit: A warren is a tangled network of tunnels or passages, a maze in which one easily gets lost.

clue.text: Deposit with investment returns already

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: to sit something somewhere is to set it down
an ISA is an Individual Savings Account, a UK tax-free investment

explanation.surface: A cash deposit bundled with an investment yields its returns straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used for 'already' in sentences like 'we're short of time as it is', meaning even now.

clue.text: Turkey's peak linked to, say, Persian area tunnel

parts.note: a Persian is a breed of cat; say marks it as an example
A is the abbreviation for area
the comb is the fleshy crest on top of a fowl's head

explanation.surface: A summit in Turkey is connected to a district of Persia by a tunnel.
explanation.walkthrough: Turkey and Persian look like countries, but one is a bird and the other a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground burial gallery is a network of subterranean passages, so it can be called a tunnel.

clue.text: Figure to get hack's sound support, first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved round to the end of the word

parts.note: a hack is a riding horse, and a horse's call is this
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A journalist hopes to get backing for a story that sounds right, putting the top item at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Hack suggests a journalist, but here it is a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure is a number, and this is the number between seventeen and nineteen.

clue.text: Pop that sounds less accessible for driving to?

indicators.note: sounds tells us to go by how a word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a place further away is harder to drive to; in British speech the R is silent

explanation.surface: Dad lives further away, which makes him harder to visit by car.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone relies on non-rhotic British pronunciation, where the R before a consonant is not sounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is an informal, chiefly American, name for one's dad, a male parent.

clue.text: Dignitary giving service in times past? On the contrary

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, though the direction is about to be flipped
on the contrary reverses the stated relationship, so the outer piece goes inside instead

parts.note: Mass is a church service
yore means long ago, as in days of yore

explanation.surface: A civic official is described as having served in an earlier era, then the claim is retracted.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the service sits in times past; 'on the contrary' turns it round so the past sits in the service.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who holds civic office as head of a town council is a local dignitary.

clue.text: Plugs damage beer barrel with metal inside

definitions.note: plural noun defining a mass noun

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage

indicators.note: inside means within, so the metal is placed in the middle of the barrel

parts.note: a keg is a small barrel for beer
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Someone stops up a beer barrel badly, with a metal stopper stuck in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Plugs looks like stoppers, but it means promotions, as when a guest plugs a new book.
explanation.definitionFit: Plugs are pieces of promotion or advertising, the activity of promoting products to buyers.

clue.text: Hear of record number seeing solo tango

indicators.note: only a single tango is allowed, so where two would meet one is dropped

parts.note: to list is to record, and a list is a record
ten is a number

explanation.surface: We learn of a record-breaking dance number featuring a lone tango.
explanation.walkthrough: Tango is T in the NATO alphabet; joined, the two pieces would have a double T, but only one is allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: To hear can mean to pay attention to sound, the act of attending with one's ears.

clue.text: Really a popular time for regular broadcast

parts.note: so means really, as in so good
taken as written
pop is short for popular
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's scheduler says a certain slot is a hugely popular one for a regular programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A serial drama shown several times a week for years is the archetypal recurring television or radio programme.

clue.text: Regret consuming Double Diamonds with Romeo — one's usually in stern control

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the last piece is simply added on
something consuming another swallows it up, so it goes around it

parts.note: to rue is to regret
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games; double gives two
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone regrets downing Double Diamond beers with Romeo, who is normally strict and controlled.
explanation.walkthrough: Double Diamond was a well-known British bottled beer. Stern means the back of a boat, not strict.
explanation.definitionFit: The steering blade of a boat is hinged at the back, so it is the control found at the stern.

clue.text: Attendees not as drunk as closer relations

indicators.note: something drunk is tipsy and disordered, so the remaining letters are jumbled
not means without, so the following little word is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: Guests who are less inebriated than their companions get on better as relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Relations looks like family members, but it means dealings between nations.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an easing of tension between rival states, bringing their diplomatic dealings nearer.

clue.text: Rip-off getting uniform for nothing — it's liable to be bent

indicators.note: X for Y means put the first in place of the second, swapping one letter

parts.note: a rip-off is daylight robbery, an overcharge
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A con involving a free uniform is the kind of scheme that crooked people go in for.
explanation.walkthrough: Bent is British slang for crooked, which suits the rip-off surface; here it means flexed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flexible and springy, like an elastic material, can easily be flexed out of shape.

clue.text: Clash, second-rate outfit playing Liverpool for instance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a conflict or failure to go together

definitions.text: second-rate outfit playing Liverpool for instance
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an unequal contest between a weak team and a top club

explanation.walkthrough: Outfit suggests clothing that clashes, but it means a team; Liverpool is a leading English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an incompatible pairing and a sporting fixture between very unequal sides.

clue.text: Caught twice holding grass, all imported by mum in score

indicators.note: holding means gripping around, so the two catches surround the next piece
imported means brought in, so everything so far goes inside the word for mum

parts.note: mum means silent, and sh is a call for silence
the second caught
a grass is an informer, as is a rat
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cricketer is caught twice holding a blade of grass, and mother brings it all into a scorebook.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum looks like mother but means silent, as in keep mum.
explanation.definitionFit: To score is to mark a surface with a line or cut, the same as making a thin mark on it.

clue.text: Representation of Monet getting born and put in grave

indicators.note: a representation renders something in a new form, so the painter's name is rearranged

parts.note: the painter's name supplies the letters
b is the abbreviation for born

explanation.surface: A portrait of the painter Monet, from his birth to his burial.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay a body to rest in a tomb or burial plot is to inter it in a grave.

clue.text: Worked backwards, 101 to 100 … after retiring, it could put you to sleep

definitions.text: it could put you to sleep

indicators.note: backwards means read from the end, so this word is turned round

parts.note: a machine that worked ran

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so this group of letters is also turned round

parts.note: CI is the Roman numeral for 101
taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Someone counting down from 101 to 100 after going to bed hopes to drift off.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers are Roman numerals, read together with the word to.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that dulls the senses and induces drowsiness can send you off into slumber.

clue.text: One rides wave on a current, rising

definitions.text: One rides wave on a current, rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so these letters are turned over
to wave is to move back and forth, so the letters of the first word are shaken up

parts.note: a, plus AC for alternating current
taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A boat or surfer is carried along on the swell of a rising stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition. 'On' in a down clue means placed below, so the jumbled word sits under the upturned current.
explanation.definitionFit: A light paddled boat carried along on a flowing river, riding the waves, fits the whole description.

clue.text: Green duck trapped by local copper

indicators.note: something trapped is shut in, so it sits between the other two pieces

parts.note: a local is a person's neighbourhood pub, an inn
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O
a copper is a low-value coin, such as a cent

explanation.surface: An inexperienced duck is caught by the neighbourhood police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like a police officer but is a coin; a local is British for one's regular pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means naive and inexperienced, unworldly and unsuspecting, just as the answer does.

clue.text: Repeatedly secure personal ornament

indicators.note: repeatedly asks for the next word to be used twice, with two different synonyms

parts.note: to tie is to make secure
to pin is also to make secure

explanation.surface: An instruction to fasten something again and again, with a decorative item.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative clip worn on a necktie is a piece of jewellery adorning a man's outfit.

clue.text: While cutting old rocker's quiff may appear thus

indicators.note: something cutting into another goes inside it, splitting it apart

parts.note: old people are often grey-haired
as can mean while, as in 'as I was leaving'

explanation.surface: While getting a haircut, an aging rocker's quiff looks a particular way.
explanation.walkthrough: Rockers were a 1960s British youth group of leather-clad motorcyclists with slicked-back hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiff slicked into place with hair oil or Brylcreem looks shiny and oily.

clue.text: Drill making that woman's revolutionary listening aids echo

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so this pronoun is read backwards

parts.note: her is the pronoun for that woman
we listen with our ears
Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A revolutionary woman's hearing aids produce a feedback echo during a drill.
explanation.definitionFit: To drill is to practise repeatedly in preparation, which is to run through something before performing.
